dissertation: Koziol, N. A. (2015). A comparison of population-averaged and cluster-specific approaches in the context of unequal probabilities of selection (Doctoral dissertation). University of Nebraska-Lincoln. Chair: James A. Bovaird. https://digitalcommons.unl.edu/cehsdiss/229/

replicated_work.title: A Comparison of Population-Averaged and Cluster-Specific Approaches in the Context of Unequal Probabilities of Selection
replicated_work.verification_locator: Title page and abstract of source/koziol2015.pdf; adviser James A. Bovaird on the title page

sections.exclusion_reason: Literature review. The operational weight formulas used in the simulation are inventoried with Chapter III.
External NCES sizes used to motivate the fixed population size. Not a performance result.

inventory_audit.reviewer: source reading of the archived dissertation PDF
inventory_audit.rationale: The PDF was read from the title page through Appendix F. Chapter I states the three research questions and Table 1.1. Chapter II is background. Chapter III and Appendix A define the design. Chapter IV, Chapter V, and Appendices C-F hold the Monte Carlo results. Acknowledgements, the bibliography, and Appendix B do not add a performance result. Bernoulli and random-coefficient results are entered as blocked claims rather than omitted.

claims.statement: Under informative sampling, a normal random-intercept outcome, intraclass correlation .05, and average cluster size 5, the intercept bias of weighted multilevel pseudo-maximum likelihood exceeds the intercept bias of weighted single-level estimation with sandwich standard errors.
claims.source_locator: Dissertation Table C.2, informative random-intercept panel, normal outcome, rho=.05, nj=5; discussion pp. 149-152
claims.conditions: Normal random-intercept model; informative Poisson design; rho=.05; target average cluster size 5; 1,000 requested replications; 998 retained after dropping nonconverged draws.

contrasts.definition: wtm.ccs intercept bias minus ws.ics intercept bias
contrasts.positive_means: weighted multilevel has a larger positive intercept bias than weighted single-level

claims.reproduction_deviation: ours minus printed contrast = 0.0010312 outcome units
claims.methods: Mplus 7 MPML with WTSCALE=CLUSTER and MLR, reconstructed as a Gaussian pseudo-likelihood with Method 2 scaling and a cluster sandwich, checked against WeMix on one production replicate.
claims.uncertainty: Paired Monte Carlo standard error of the contrast is 0.000416. The printed contrast is treated as exact in that band and also allowed a half-thousandth extraction bound. Original Monte Carlo error is not in the dissertation.
claims.multiplicity: One prespecified primary contrast. Unadjusted. Not an equivalence test.
claims.status_reason: The contrast is positive in both sources. The gap of 0.001 is one unit in the last printed place. It is just outside two of our standard errors if 0.151 is exact, and inside that interval once the printed number is allowed its half-thousandth rounding range. The estimator order is unchanged.
claims.numerical: close at the printed thousandth for the contrast; the raw multilevel bias 0.153 against 0.151 is a mismatch at that precision
claims.reconstruction_scope: limited reconstruction in R, not Mplus 7 and not the original seed stream
limitations: Bernoulli and random-coefficient settings were not rerun.
The raw multilevel bias misses the printed thousandth by 0.002.

stopping.attempted: Full normal random-intercept factorial at 1,000 requested draws, plus a WeMix cross-check.
stopping.resource_basis: One informative cell of this size took about five minutes on three cores.
stopping.next_evidence: Mplus output for this cell would separate sandwich scaling from Monte Carlo error.

claims.statement: Under the same informative cell, approximate cluster weights leave a larger intercept bias than the true multilevel weights.
claims.source_locator: Dissertation Table C.2, wam.ccs versus wtm.ccs, informative, normal, rho=.05, nj=5; Research question 3, pp. 154-155
claims.conditions: Same cell as C1. Approximate cluster weight is M divided by the realized number of clusters, and the conditional weight is the unconditional weight divided by that constant.

contrasts.definition: wam.ccs intercept bias minus wtm.ccs intercept bias
contrasts.positive_means: approximate weights leave a larger positive intercept bias than true multilevel weights

claims.reproduction_deviation: ours minus printed contrast = -0.0007767 outcome units
claims.methods: Kovacevic-Rai cluster-weight approximation as coded in Appendix A, then the same pseudo-likelihood as C1.
claims.uncertainty: Paired Monte Carlo standard error 0.000515. Inside two standard errors and inside the 0.001 rounding tolerance.
claims.multiplicity: One prespecified contrast for the approximate-weight headline. Unadjusted.
claims.status_reason: Both contrasts are positive and agree within the rounding tolerance and within two Monte Carlo standard errors.
limitations: The approximation was evaluated on the normal random-intercept grid only.

stopping.resource_basis: Included in the same run as C1.
stopping.next_evidence: No further run is required for this normal cell.

claims.statement: Under the same informative cell, weighted single-level sandwich intervals cover the intercept at about the nominal rate and weighted multilevel intervals do not.
claims.source_locator: Dissertation Table E.2, informative, normal, rho=.05, nj=5
claims.conditions: Same cell as C1. Coverage is the proportion of Wald intervals using 1.96 standard errors.

contrasts.definition: ws.ics intercept coverage minus wtm.ccs intercept coverage
contrasts.positive_means: weighted single-level intervals cover more often than weighted multilevel intervals

claims.methods: Survey cluster-robust standard errors for the single-level fit and the observed pseudo-likelihood sandwich for the multilevel fit.
claims.uncertainty: Binomial standard error of a coverage near .95 with 998 draws is about 0.007. The printed difference and ours agree in the third decimal.
claims.multiplicity: One coverage contrast at the primary cell. The nj=20 coverage gap is a separate supporting claim.
claims.status_reason: Both sources give a coverage gap of 0.945 at three decimals, and both show multilevel coverage at the intercept of essentially zero.
claims.reconstruction_scope: limited reconstruction; sandwich finite-sample scaling may differ from Mplus MLR
limitations: Unweighted multilevel standard errors in this study are model-based rather than MLR.

stopping.untested: Mplus MLR standard errors on the same samples.
stopping.next_evidence: Mplus standard-error output for this cell.

claims.statement: Under an informative design and a Bernoulli outcome, weighted multilevel probit pseudo-maximum likelihood is more biased for the intercept than weighted single-level probit estimation.
claims.source_locator: Dissertation Table C.2, informative, Bernoulli, rho=.05, nj=5, gamma00 column

ours.unavailable_reason: The Bernoulli arm was not rerun. One probit quadrature fit did not converge and was not used as evidence.

claims.conditions: Random-intercept probit, informative design, rho=.05, average cluster size 5. Expected as part of the 208 settings. Completed: none.

contrasts.definition: wtm.ccs intercept bias minus ws.ics intercept bias
contrasts.positive_means: weighted multilevel has a larger signed intercept bias than weighted single-level

claims.methods: Not run. Mplus used LINK=PROBIT. WeMix 4.0.3 binomial models use the logit link.
claims.multiplicity: Not entered into the Gaussian family of tests.
claims.status_reason: The comparison was not computed. A nonconverged single draw is not a Monte Carlo result.
limitations: The dissertation headline about non-normal outcomes is not established here.

stopping.reason: Stopped before a Bernoulli production run.
stopping.attempted: One 21-node probit fit that did not converge; WeMix inspected and found to be logit-only.
stopping.untested: The 1,000-replication Bernoulli grid and the random-coefficient grid.

claims.statement: Under non-informative sampling and a normal random-intercept outcome, unweighted and weighted estimators of the intercept are all within about two thousandths of zero.
claims.conditions: Four non-informative normal random-intercept cells. Published cell entries are between -0.002 and 0.001. Our cell means are between -0.002 and 0.002.

contrasts.definition: largest absolute intercept bias across the four non-informative cells and five estimators, ours minus the largest absolute printed bias
contrasts.positive_means: our largest absolute bias exceeds the largest absolute printed bias

claims.reproduction_deviation: both maxima are 0.002 at three decimals
claims.methods: Same estimators as the informative cells.
claims.uncertainty: Biases this small are within a few Monte Carlo standard errors of zero. Relative bias is undefined at a zero intercept.
claims.multiplicity: Descriptive summary of 20 non-informative intercept means, not a 20-test family with a correction.
claims.status_reason: Every non-informative intercept mean is within two thousandths of zero, which is the pattern in Table C.1.
limitations: The published value stored here is the largest absolute printed bias in the panel, not a single cell.

stopping.untested: Nothing further for this normal panel.
stopping.next_evidence: No further evidence is required for the normal non-informative intercepts.

claims.statement: The realized sample under the primary cell has about 968 clusters and about 4,884 students, with mean cluster weight about 50.
claims.source_locator: Dissertation Table 4.1, informative or non-informative random-intercept column, rho=.05, nj=5
claims.conditions: Primary informative cell, mean over 998 retained replications.

contrasts.definition: our mean cluster count minus the published mean cluster count

claims.reproduction_deviation: ours minus published mean cluster count = 3.648
claims.uncertainty: The published mean is over her 1,000 replications. A difference of about four clusters on a mean of 964 is under one percent.
claims.multiplicity: One design-moment check, not a performance family.
claims.status_reason: Sample size, cluster count, and weight moments agree with Table 4.1 at the precision that table uses for those moments.
claims.numerical: mismatch at the printed cluster count, within one percent
limitations: Cluster count is a mean of random Poisson samples, so exact equality is not expected.

stopping.reason: Design moments were recorded for every replicate.
stopping.next_evidence: Her saved samples would show whether the four-cluster gap is only seed noise.

claims.statement: At average cluster size 20 and intraclass correlation .05, true-weight multilevel coverage of the intercept is well below nominal but higher than at cluster size 5.
claims.source_locator: Dissertation Table E.2, informative, normal, rho=.05, nj=20, wtm.ccs gamma00
claims.conditions: Informative normal random-intercept, rho=.05, nj=20, 965 retained replications.

contrasts.definition: our coverage minus the published coverage

claims.methods: Same sandwich as C3. A five percent larger standard error would move coverage to about 0.288.
claims.uncertainty: Our binomial standard error is about 0.014. Her standard error at 1,000 draws is about 0.014. The gap is inside two standard errors of the difference and just outside two standard errors that use only ours.
claims.multiplicity: One supporting cell, reported because it is the largest coverage gap. Not a corrected test.
claims.status_reason: Both numbers show substantial undercoverage. They do not agree at the printed thousandth.
limitations: Standard-error scaling relative to Mplus MLR is unresolved.

stopping.attempted: 1,000 requested replications and a standard-error scale check.
stopping.untested: Mplus standard errors on the same samples.
stopping.next_evidence: Mplus MLR standard errors for this cell.

synthesis: Partly replicated. On the normal random-intercept grid, weighted single-level sandwich estimation recovers the intercept and weighted multilevel pseudo-maximum likelihood does not, and approximate cluster weights are worse under informative designs. The primary contrast is 0.152 against the printed 0.151. Bernoulli and random-coefficient arms were not rerun.
limitations: C4: Bernoulli settings were not rerun, so the non-normal part of the headline is not established.
C7: Random-coefficient settings were not rerun.
C1: The raw multilevel intercept bias is 0.153 against the printed 0.151.
C8: True-weight multilevel coverage at cluster size 20 and intraclass correlation .05 is 0.248 against 0.282.
Original Mplus 7 input and replicate files were not obtained, so seeds and the MLR scaling are unresolved.
